cards.text: Jesus is still teaching, and now He tells them a parable. Luke gives us the point BEFORE the story even starts, like reading the recipe card before touching the dough. I have never once done that.

cards.question: Luke says Jesus tells this parable about their need to do what?

answers.text: Pray at all times and not lose heart
Give to the poor and not grow weary
Keep watch and not fall asleep

cards.text: The parable opens in a certain town, with a judge who neither feared God nor respected men. Friend, that man isn't just unbothered, he's PROFESSIONALLY unbothered.
In that town there's a widow who keeps appealing to him: 'Give me justice against my adversary.' Same widow, same line, over and over.

cards.question: The judge gives the widow justice the first time she asks.

cards.text: For a while he refuses. Then later he talks to himself, and he's honest: he still doesn't fear God or respect men, but something is getting to him.

cards.question: The judge says he'll give the widow justice because she keeps ___ him.
If the judge doesn't give the widow justice, what does he say she'll do?

answers.text: Wear him out with her requests
Tell the whole town about him
Take her case to the king

cards.text: She didn't win with a better argument, she won with the SAME one, again and again. That's the alarm clock beating the snooze button: it never gets smarter, it just never stops.
Then the Lord says, 'Listen to the words of the unjust judge.' And now Jesus sets that judge right next to God.

cards.question: Jesus asks if God will bring about justice for those who cry out to Him day and night. Who does Jesus call them?
Jesus asks if God will delay in helping them. Then He says God will ___ carry out justice on their behalf.

cards.text: That judge had to be worn down like a stuck drawer, and trust me, friend, I KNOW stuck drawers. But Jesus says God won't delay.

cards.question: Jesus ends with a question about when the Son of Man comes. Will He find what on earth?

cards.text: Jesus tells another parable, aimed at some who viewed others with contempt. I read that and thought, 'Good thing that's not ME,' and then I heard myself.

cards.question: Luke says the people this parable is for trusted in what?
In the parable, two men go up to the temple to pray. One is a Pharisee. Who is the other?

cards.text: The Pharisee stands by himself and prays. He starts out thanking God, so far, so good.

cards.question: What does the Pharisee thank God for?

answers.text: That he is not like other men

cards.text: Then he lists them: swindlers, evildoers, adulterers, 'or even like this tax collector.' Friend, he came to talk to God and spent the whole time talking about the other guy.

cards.question: Next, the Pharisee confesses his own sins to God.

cards.text: Instead, he tells God he fasts twice a week and pays tithes of all he acquires. He walked into prayer like a job interview, and somehow HE'S the one doing the hiring.

cards.question: Now the tax collector. He stood at a ___ to pray.

cards.text: He won't even lift up his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beats his breast.

cards.question: Eyes down, beating his breast, what does the tax collector pray?

answers.text: God have mercy on me a sinner
God I have done my very best
God I am better than that man

cards.text: Seven words. No list, no résumé, no review of the other guy, just 'God, have mercy on me, a sinner!'

cards.question: Jesus says the Pharisee is the one who went home justified.
Jesus says everyone who ___ himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be ___.

cards.text: The man who asked for mercy went home justified, not the man who praised himself. Friend, I spent years at the bottom of a junk drawer, and I can tell you: the bottom is a GREAT place to get found.

findings.problem: The opening card says Jesus tells 'them' a parable but never says who 'them' is. The context in Luke 17:22 is His disciples. The opening card has to say who is being spoken to.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'ignoring' isn't believable. Card 4 has just told the baker that the widow keeps appealing to the judge, so 'she keeps ignoring him' contradicts a fact already given.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish. Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new. It goes back over Luke 18:5, which cards 7 and 8 already covered, only to carry a joke. It doesn't move the baker forward through the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. It repeats that the judge was worn down (cards 6 to 9) and that God won't delay (card 12), and it adds no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The card says the Pharisee 'spent the whole time talking about the other guy.' The text shows this isn't so: in Luke 18:12 he goes on to talk about his own fasting and tithes, which card 8 then tells. The line states something the text shows is wrong.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The job interview joke doesn't click. A candidate listing his qualifications fits the image, but 'HE'S the one doing the hiring' leaves the baker asking who he is hiring. If the answer is God, the joke edges toward making God the one being interviewed.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The wrong answers don't fit the blank 'stood at a ___'. 'At a altar' and 'at a front' don't read naturally, so 'distance' is the only answer that sounds right and stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. It repeats the tax collector's prayer, which card 11 just answered, and adds no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. It repeats that the tax collector, not the Pharisee, went home justified, which card 13 already answered, and adds no new part of the passage.
